transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-07
Time: 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE); Miguel Ortega (Redwood CSM); Samir Patel (Redwood SE); Daniel Kwan (Zenith Eng); Priya Rao (Zenith Platform); Ellen Park (Zenith Security); Markus Lind (Zenith DevOps)

Summary:
Quick kickoff for implementation ramp, align SLA targets, network/VPC intake, compliance docs, and initial benchmarking plan. Customer wants predictable latency <150ms p50 for 512-token prompts and clear data residency and audit log commitments. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and a phased pilot.

Topics covered:
- High-level ramp plan and timeline
- Network/VPC and private connectivity requirements
- SLA and SLO targets (latency, availability, error budgets)
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2/ISO/KMS) and retention of logs
- Benchmarks (prompt set, concurrency, token distribution)
- Next steps and owners

Action items (captured above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone thanks for making time, we'll go quick — I'm Laura with Redwood, with Miguel and Samir. Uh, want to run objectives for today's kickoff, make sure we have the right owners and first week milestones.
[00:18] Daniel Kwan: Yep thanks Laura. From Zenith side we've got Priya, Ellen, Markus — goal here is to validate we can hit our latency and also satisfy security/compliance requirements before we push to pilot.
[00:33] Miguel Ortega: Quick intro from my side — I'll be your CSM, main contact for timelines, billing liaison, escalations.
[00:41] Samir Patel: And I'm Samir, SE — I'll own the performance bench and the initial integration run.
[00:47] Priya Rao: Quick question — for the pilot we expect about 200 concurrent sessions with peak bursts to 500, are we talking Dedicated or Hosted for that?
[00:57] Samir Patel: Good question. So Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and isolation, Hosted can work but you'll see variance on p95 during bursts unless we configure reserved capacity or autoscaling. There's a mid path — reserved Dedicated pool with burst back to hosted for overflow, we've done that for payments customers before.
[01:20] Ellen Park: From security we need to see SOC2 reports, KMS integration details, and audit log retention. Also, data never leaves EU for EU customers — does Redwood support region pinning?
[01:33] Laura Chen: Yes region pinning supported; for Private deployments we can do VPC and on-prem variants. We'll share our SOC2 report and a doc for KMS flow. Note: some of the product names in our docs get OOV transcriptions, sorry if the auto-doc says Redwood-thing, we'll clarify.
[01:49] Markus Lind: On the network side we're planning an AWS Transit Gateway peering into our account, need to confirm egress IPs and firewall rules.
[01:58] Samir Patel: We'll provide an infra checklist — IP ranges, ports (TLS 443 outbound, and optionally for private we do a VPC endpoint), and the CIDR ranges. I'll own the network walkthrough with Markus.
[02:13] Daniel Kwan: For SLOs, our business wants p50 <150ms on 512-token inference and p95 <400ms. Is that realistic?
[02:23] Samir Patel: Depends on model selection and quantization profile. On modern LLMs we can hit p50 ~80-130ms with optimized kernels on A100/RTX-class GPU and batching tuned. We'll need your prompt distribution and a sample corpus for bench. We'll run a baseline and then iterate quant+batch settings.
[02:43] Priya Rao: We have a mix of 128–1024 token prompts, avg around 512. We'll put together a sample set — is there a preferred format?
[02:51] Samir Patel: JSONL with prompt and expected tokens per request works best. Also include desired stop sequences.
[02:58] Miguel Ortega: Let's capture that as an action: Samir to run bench, Laura to share runbook, Ellen to send SOC2 items.
[03:08] Ellen Park: Also need to know about log retention and where logs land — do you redact PII by default?
[03:15] Laura Chen: By default logs are retained per plan, and we can do automatic redaction rules or forward logs to your SIEM via S3 or syslog. We'll include the options in the runbook.
[03:27] Daniel Kwan: We also have concerns about hallucination / model quality — we want to lock model versions and have rollback policies. How are rollouts handled?
[03:36] Samir Patel: Redwood supports pinning model versions and rollout strategies: canaries, A/B, auto-fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes. We'll propose a canary plan for the pilot.
[03:48] Priya Rao: Cost is also a big factor — can we get a ballpark for dedicated monthly commit vs hosted per-token?
[03:55] Laura Chen: We'll send a T-shirt sizing and pricing spreadsheet. Roughly, reserved Dedicated is more predictable but requires a commit; hosted is elastic but can be higher per token at scale. We'll include cost per 1M tokens and a modeled estimate for your expected traffic in the follow-up.
[04:13] Markus Lind: Back to networking, we need an exact list of egress IPs and TLS cert fingerprinting, otherwise our firewall team won't approve.
[04:21] Samir Patel: We'll include IP ranges and certificate thumbprints; for VPC private link options we can avoid egress IPs entirely.
[04:29] Ellen Park: On KMS — we want customer-managed keys, not vendor-managed. Is that supported?
[04:35] Laura Chen: Yes, customer-managed KMS supported for Private and Dedicated, for hosted we can integrate with your KMS via an exchange for keys. We'll flag any limitations in the doc.
[04:45] Daniel Kwan: Ok timeline-wise we want pilot in mid-June and production late July — is that feasible?
[04:53] Miguel Ortega: Feasible if we hit two gates: network + compliance sign-off by end of May, and bench + small pilot test the first two weeks of June.
[05:03] Laura Chen: Proposed immediate next steps: Laura sends runbook+SSO doc; Samir schedules bench and network call; Ellen provides compliance list; we sync in one week for a readiness check.
[05:13] Priya Rao: One more operational question — token-level cost visibility and per-route dashboards, is that in the Console?
[05:20] Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, token breakdowns, tracing and per-model latency histograms — we'll demo that in the next session.
[05:29] (brief crosstalk, someone on muted line)
[05:36] Daniel Kwan: Fine. Can you also share any PCI-specific controls? Payments need more than SOC2.
[05:42] Ellen Park: Yes we'll need the PCI support details and whether Redwood can be in-scope or out-of-scope for our PCI attestation.
[05:48] Laura Chen: We'll include a PCI artifact list and our recommendations — note some customers keep the inference layer out-of-scope by tokenizing and truncating sensitive fields upstream. We'll add engineering patterns to the runbook.
[05:59] Miguel Ortega: I'll set the follow-up: a readiness check next Friday (2026-05-14) and a network deep-dive with Markus for 2026-05-11.
[06:08] Samir Patel: I'll kick off the benchmark once we get the JSONL prompt set and an IAM account for benching or a signed NDA if needed for sample data.
[06:17] Daniel Kwan: Great — thanks everyone.
[06:22] Laura Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.

Recap (end):
- Send runbook, SSO guidance, PCI/SOC2 artifacts (Laura) — due 2026-05-10.
- Samir to run baseline bench with provided prompt set and propose Dedicated sizing — due 2026-05-14.
- Network deep-dive with Markus to confirm IPs/CIDR and firewall rules — scheduled 2026-05-11 (pending invite).
- Ellen to send compliance artifact list and requirements — due 2026-05-12.

References shared in call:
- Link: Redwood Implementation Runbook (to be sent)
- Link: Reserved Capacity T-shirt sizing spreadsheet (to be sent)
- Note: customers often refer to 'Redwood Dedicated' as 'red- dedicated' in auto transcripts (typo in past exports).
